Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We're ready to move forward but need to get the DPA finalized before procurement signs the SOW. Our counsel redlined a couple of items that are sticking points for security & compliance:

1) Backup/DR carve-out: Pioneer requires that encrypted backups and crash-consistent snapshots used solely for disaster recovery may be held for operational purposes beyond the primary retention period. They asked for an explicit carve-out allowing up to 180 days in backups for encrypted snapshots and a 365-day tombstone retention for metadata required for legal hold, with a commitment to expedited deletion where reasonably possible.

2) Subprocessors: 30-day notice of new subprocessors and an ability to object for regulated data (healthcare PHI adjacent).

3) EU->US transfer references: they'd like to see a specific cross-border transfer mechanism called out and the subprocessor list attached as an exhibit.

I've attached our redline (Pioneer_DPA_v1_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether we can sign via DocuSign once we align? Procurement would like a final DocuSign envelope by next Wednesday.

Regards,
Amelia Ward

Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA - Pioneer preferred language on backups/DR and subprocessors

Rachel/Laura —

Quick technical notes on the backup/DR ask:

- Our managed backup flow is snapshot-based and encrypted at rest. Snapshots are kept as immutable objects for 90 days by default; we can extend snapshot retention on a per-account basis up to 180 days but that is an operational opt-in and increases storage costs.
- Tombstone/metadata: object stores and DB tombstones can remain discoverable for longer due to lifecycle and eventual consistency; practical upper bound without manual remediation is ~180 days. Holding items longer (365 days) is doable only if we create a dedicated retention bucket and apply extra controls — we'd want Pioneer to cover the incremental cost and accept that those items may be subject to disaster recovery processes.
- Deletion guarantee: we cannot promise deletion from third-party storage providers within a fixed short window; we can commit to taking commercially reasonable steps to purge and provide attestations once completed.

Suggested language (short):
"For disaster recovery purposes, encrypted backups and crash-consistent snapshots may be retained for up to 180 days. Tombstone and metadata related to legal hold or restoration may be retained up to 180 days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove Customer Data from backups and DR copies following deletion from the primary environment and will provide written confirmation upon completion."

If Pioneer insists on 365 days for tombstones, we should require it in writing and include a cost/recovery schedule.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-18T13:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA - Pioneer preferred language on backups/DR and subprocessors

Thanks — see proposed redline below. I've tried to balance Pioneer compliance asks with our operational realities: keep the carve-out tight, avoid open-ended retention windows, and preserve the "commercially reasonable efforts" deletion standard we use elsewhere.

Proposed redline text to send back to Pioneer (attached also in redline_Redwood_DPA_v2026-12-18.pdf):

"Backup and Disaster Recovery. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Customer Data contained in encrypted backups, immutable crash-consistent snapshots, or other copies created solely for redundancy and disaster recovery purposes (collectively, 'Backups') may be retained for operational purposes for up to one hundred and eighty (180) days following creation. Notwithstanding the foregoing, metadata necessary to support legal hold or restoration operations may be retained for up to one hundred and eighty (180) days unless otherwise agreed in writing, in which case additional retention will require written authorization and separate pricing. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to purge Customer Data from Backups upon written request following deletion from active systems and will provide written confirmation when purge operations are reasonably completed.

Subprocessors and Notice. Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors at [link to subprocessor exhibit] and will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' notice of any new subprocessor. Customer may object in writing on reasonable grounds relating to GDPR/health data compliance; failure to reach agreement will be addressed under the escalation procedure in Section X.

Cross-border Transfers. The Parties acknowledge the use of appropriate transfer mechanisms for data transfers from the EEA to the United States (e.g., SCCs or other lawful mechanism) and will reflect the appropriate mechanism in an annex or exhibit to this DPA where applicable.

Execution. We prefer DocuSign for execution; please provide an envelope or confirm if Pioneer uses AdobeSign and we'll accommodate.

Next steps: Rachel — if you're comfortable with this position I'll send the redline and DocuSign envelope request back to Amelia. If Pioneer pushes for 365 days for tombstones, we should require written confirmation from their DPO and a discussion about cost.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
